messages.subject: process: hotfix branches
parts:
[moving to stan-dev]

Ben, can you weigh in?

I don't think I can foresee how this one's going to play out. I think the simpler process is to not work on hotfixes for this release, but that may not be the best decision in the future. We could always postpone the process-level decision. For this release, I think we shouldn't have hotfixes since we've done so much and it'd be a PAIN to merge into both v1.3.0 and develop.


Daniel



On Thu, May 23, 2013 at 1:26 PM, Bob Carpenter <notifi...@github.com> wrote:
We plan to use hotfix branches not for generic bug fixes,
but for patches we want to apply to the latest release
to do an intermediate release. Since we don't anticipate
a patch release before 2.0, we shouldn't be creating hotfixes.

We could change that policy so that the latest 'master' branch
just has hotfix bug fixes, but we don't actually go all the
way through with an official release. That is, we branch from
latest master onto hotfix/bug#, fix the bug, merge back into
master, bump the version number of master and tag it, but don't
announce the release. This would allow people to get our latest
master as the most recently patched version.

Thoughts?

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: process: hotfix branches
parts:
On Thursday, May 23, 2013 11:03:25 PM UTC-4, Daniel Lee wrote:
I don't think I can foresee how this one's going to play out. I think the simpler process is to not work on hotfixes for this release, but that may not be the best decision in the future. We could always postpone the process-level decision. For this release, I think we shouldn't have hotfixes since we've done so much and it'd be a PAIN to merge into both v1.3.0 and develop.
I agree at the moment we are in a weird situation because develop is so far ahead of master. That said ...

On Thu, May 23, 2013 at 1:26 PM, Bob Carpenter <notifi...@github.com> wrote:
We plan to use hotfix branches not for generic bug fixes,
but for patches we want to apply to the latest release
to do an intermediate release. Since we don't anticipate
a patch release before 2.0, we shouldn't be creating hotfixes.

By definition, we never anticipate the need for a hotfix. However, should a severe enough bug arise, then I guess we would have to. What is the bug in question?

Also, how much human effort is going to be necessary to do a hotfix release? Isn't it pretty much

-- write a release note into the hotfix branch
-- merge into master (and develop)
-- make dist
-- update website

I could see an official release with a release branch as being somewhat more involved.

We could change that policy so that the latest 'master' branch
just has hotfix bug fixes, but we don't actually go all the
way through with an official release.

Again I am wondering what is the cost to an official hotfix release? There is some cost to confusing users as to what is or is not official with posts on stan-users that say "If you want to avoid this bug, use this git command ...".

Ben
